scope: Independently encoded TCP peer; actual RabbitMQ integration is separate.
tests: recovery configuration validation precedes connection creation
ordered cross-channel topology and server-named queue aliases survive repeated disconnects
deliveries received during recovery wait for readiness and stale tags never reach new channel
unconfirmed publications reject and are not silently republished after recovery
soft channel error recovers that channel without disconnecting a healthy sibling
deleted topology, unbound routes and cancelled consumers are not resurrected
transient mode preserves subscriptions but skips durable declarations
disabled topology still restores channel QoS and transaction mode
skippable topology failure reopens channel before restoring remaining entities
topology error callback can refuse skipping and exhaust retry budget
connection failure during topology replay retries the complete recovery sequence
explicit close cancels retry delay without creating another socket
AbortSignal cancels a reconnect handshake and releases the wait
ready wait cancellation is local and callback errors do not stop recovery listeners
topology stores an independent argument snapshot and enforces a bounded registry
pending non-idempotent RPC rejects instead of being replayed after reconnect
failure of the last topology entity still leaves a usable reopened channel
skipping a failed consumer restores earlier subscriptions after reopening its channel
broker consumer cancellation removes its recovery entry
closing a channel during connection recovery cannot resurrect or leak the opening channel
connection recovery supersedes an older channel retry without a duplicate open
server-named queue aliases also work for later passive declarations
closing connection from a channel ready listener cannot resurrect it
closing connection from stateChange suppresses stale readiness notifications
a channel recovery notification permits a new topology RPC
